paragraphs.text: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν πλουσίους.
paragraphs.translit: Anablepsas de eiden tous ballontas eis to gazophylakion ta dōra autōn plousious.

i18n.en: Looking up, he saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.

paragraphs.text: εἶδεν δέ τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ λεπτὰ δύο,
paragraphs.translit: eiden de tina chēran penichran ballousan ekei lepta dyo,

i18n.en: And he saw a certain poor widow putting in two lepta there,

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· Alēthōs legō hymin hoti hē chēra hautē hē ptōchē pleion pantōn ebalen·

i18n.en: and he said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them;

paragraphs.text: πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
paragraphs.translit: pantes gar houtoi ek tou perisseuontos autois ebalon eis ta dōra, hautē de ek tou hysterēmatos autēs panta ton bion hon eichen ebalen.

i18n.en: for all these contributed out of their abundance to the gifts, but she, out of her poverty, put in all the livelihood that she had."

paragraphs.text: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται, εἶπεν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai tinōn legontōn peri tou hierou, hoti lithois kalois kai anathēmasin kekosmētai, eipen·

i18n.en: And as some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and votive offerings, he said,

notes.official: The Temple-discourse opening at Lk 21:5-7 sets up the Lukan Olivet Discourse. The Temple's *kalois lithois kai anathēmasin* 'fine stones and dedicatory-offerings' was the architectural and ritual focus of late-Second-Temple-period Jewish religious life; Herod the Great's Temple-expansion (begun c. 20-19 BCE) had produced an architectural marvel widely-recognized in Greco-Roman antiquity (Josephus War 5.184-247; Tacitus Histories 5.8.1).

paragraphs.text: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: Tauta ha theōreite, eleusontai hēmerai en hais ouk aphethēsetai lithos epi lithō hos ou katalythēsetai.

i18n.en: "As for these things that you see, the days will come when there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down."

notes.official: *lithos epi lithō* 'stone upon stone' — vivid demolition-prediction. The prediction is widely interpreted as either (a) a vaticinium-ex-eventu post-70-CE Lukan composition (the dominant historical-critical view: Bovon Hermeneia, Fitzmyer AB, Nolland WBC); or (b) an authentic-Jesus-prediction of imminent eschatological-temple-destruction in line with the Jeremianic and Ezekiel-prophetic tradition (Bock ECNT). The Temple was destroyed by Titus' Roman forces in 70 CE during the First Jewish War; Lk's likely composition-date in the 80s CE places the writing after the historical destruction.

paragraphs.text: ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: epērōtēsan de auton legontes· Didaskale, pote oun tauta estai, kai ti to sēmeion hotan mellē tauta ginesthai?

i18n.en: And they asked him, saying, "Teacher, when therefore will these things be, and what will be the sign when these things are about to take place?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι, καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Blepete mē planēthēte· polloi gar eleusontai epi tō onomati mou legontes· Egō eimi, kai· Ho kairos ēngiken· mē poreuthēte opisō autōn.

i18n.en: And he said, "See that you are not led astray; for many will come in my name, saying, 'I am he,' and, 'The time has drawn near.' Do not go after them.

paragraphs.text: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de akousēte polemous kai akatastasias, mē ptoēthēte· dei gar tauta genesthai prōton, all’ ouk eutheōs to telos.

i18n.en: And when you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end will not be immediately."

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,
paragraphs.translit: Tote elegen autois· Egerthēsetai ethnos ep’ ethnos kai basileia epi basileian,

i18n.en: Then he said to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;

paragraphs.text: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἔσται.
paragraphs.translit: seismoi te megaloi kai kata topous limoi kai loimoi esontai, phobētra te kai ap’ ouranou sēmeia megala estai.

i18n.en: there will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and pestilences; and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.

notes.official: The *sēmeia ... megala kai apo ouranou* 'great signs from heaven' opens the cosmic-signs cluster that the discourse will develop at vv.25-26. Cross-reference to the broader Lukan-Acts pattern of cosmic-portents accompanying eschatological-divine intervention (Acts 2:19-20 Joel-citation; Lk 23:44-45 the crucifixion-darkness + temple-curtain-tearing).

paragraphs.text: πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
paragraphs.translit: pro de toutōn pantōn epibalousin eph’ hymas tas cheiras autōn kai diōxousin, paradidontes eis tas synagōgas kai phylakas, apagomenous epi basileis kai hēgemonas heneken tou onomatos mou·

i18n.en: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to the synagogues and prisons, dragging you before kings and governors for the sake of my name.

paragraphs.text: ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.
paragraphs.translit: apobēsetai hymin eis martyrion.

i18n.en: It will result for you as a testimony.

paragraphs.text: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι,
paragraphs.translit: thete oun en tais kardiais hymōn mē promeletan apologēthēnai,

i18n.en: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to prepare your defense in advance,

paragraphs.text: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: egō gar dōsō hymin stoma kai sophian hē ou dynēsontai antistēnai ē anteipein pantes hoi antikeimenoi hymin.

i18n.en: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or contradict.

paragraphs.text: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: paradothēsesthe de kai hypo goneōn kai adelphōn kai syngenōn kai philōn, kai thanatōsousin ex hymōn,

i18n.en: You will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death;

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
paragraphs.translit: kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn dia to onoma mou.

i18n.en: and you will be hated by all because of my name.

paragraphs.text: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται.
paragraphs.translit: kai thrix ek tēs kephalēs hymōn ou mē apolētai.

i18n.en: Yet not a hair of your head will perish.

paragraphs.text: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: en tē hypomonē hymōn ktēsasthe tas psychas hymōn.

i18n.en: By your endurance gain your souls.

paragraphs.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de idēte kykloumenēn hypo stratopedōn Ierousalēm, tote gnōte hoti ēngiken hē erēmōsis autēs.

i18n.en: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has drawn near.

paragraphs.text: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,
paragraphs.translit: tote hoi en tē Ioudaia pheugetōsan eis ta orē, kai hoi en mesō autēs ekchōreitōsan, kai hoi en tais chōrais mē eiserchesthōsan eis autēn,

i18n.en: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those who are inside the city depart, and let those who are in the country not enter it;

paragraphs.text: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
paragraphs.translit: hoti hēmerai ekdikēseōs hautai eisin tou plēsthēnai panta ta gegrammena.

i18n.en: for these are days of vengeance, that all the things that are written may be fulfilled.

paragraphs.text: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,
paragraphs.translit: ouai tais en gastri echousais kai tais thēlazousais en ekeinais tais hēmerais· estai gar anankē megalē epi tēs gēs kai orgē tō laō toutō,

i18n.en: Woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing infants in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people;

paragraphs.text: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai pesountai stomati machairēs kai aichmalōtisthēsontai eis ta ethnē panta, kai Ierousalēm estai patoumenē hypo ethnōn, achri hou plērōthōsin kairoi ethnōn.

i18n.en: and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

notes.official: *kairoi ethnōn* 'times of the Gentiles' is a Lukan-distinctive eschatological-historical-framework phrase. The Jerusalem-being-trampled imagery draws on Zech 12:3 + Dan 8:13 + Isa 63:18 traditions; the *kairoi ethnōn* framework anticipates Paul's mystery-of-Israel discussion at Rom 11:25-26.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,
paragraphs.translit: Kai esontai sēmeia en hēliō kai selēnē kai astrois, kai epi tēs gēs synochē ethnōn en aporia ēchous thalassēs kai salou,

i18n.en: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth distress of nations in perplexity at the roaring of the sea and the surging waves,

notes.official: **MAJOR COSMIC-SIGNS SITE + RAËLIAN CANON CITATION.** *sēmeia en hēliō kai selēnē kai astrois* ('signs in sun and moon and stars') opens the Lukan cosmic-signs at vv.25-26. Cross-corpus chain: Joel 2:30-31 HB / 3:3-4 LXX (the foundational passage) → Isa 13:10 + Isa 34:4 + Ezek 32:7-8 + Amos 8:9 (the broader prophetic-apocalyptic substrate) → Mk 13:24-25 // Mt 24:29 (the Synoptic parallel) → Acts 2:19-20 (Peter's Joel-citation at Pentecost) → Rev 6:12-13 (the sixth-seal opening). The Lukan formulation is the most-generalized of the Synoptic versions ('signs in sun and moon and stars'); the *synochē ethnōn en aporia* ('distress of nations in perplexity') + *apopsychontōn anthrōpōn apo phobou* ('men fainting from fear') details at v.26 are Lukan-distinctive narrative additions. Documented at the central-glossary entry `cosmic-signs-cluster-joel-2-mark-13-acts-2-luke-21-rev-6-cross-corpus`. The Raëlian canon engagement is acknowledged-without-endorsement per the established framework (bidirectional with v2.60.0 Qur'an `inshiqaq-al-qamar`).

paragraphs.text: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: apopsychontōn anthrōpōn apo phobou kai prosdokias tōn eperchomenōn tē oikoumenē, hai gar dynameis tōn ouranōn saleuthēsontai.

i18n.en: people fainting with fear and with foreboding of what is coming upon the world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai tote opsontai ton huion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelē meta dynameōs kai doxēs pollēs.

i18n.en: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

notes.official: **MAJOR SON-OF-MAN VERSE — DANIELIC PAROUSIA + RAËLIAN CANON CITATION.** *ton huion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelē* 'the Son of Man coming in a cloud'. The Lukan singular *nephelē* (in a cloud) rather than the Markan plural is one of the most-discussed Lukan editorial decisions — likely echoing the Acts 1:9-11 Ascension *nephelē* (Jesus ascends in a singular cloud and will return *en nephelē*), establishing a Lukan-Acts literary-Christological integration between the ascension and the parousia. Cross-corpus chain: Dan 7:13-14 (the Aramaic source-text) → Mk 13:26 + Mt 24:30 + Lk 21:27 (the Synoptic Olivet Discourses) → Mk 14:62 + Mt 26:64 + Lk 22:69 (the Sanhedrin trial) → Rev 1:7 (the Apocalypse opening). The verse integrates the Lukan singular *nephelē* with the Danielic enthronement-figure tradition. Documented at the central-glossary entries `son-of-man-coming-in-cloud-dan-7-13-synoptic-revelation-1-7-cross-corpus` and `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`. The Raëlian-canon engagement is acknowledged-without-endorsement per the established framework.

paragraphs.text: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: archomenōn de toutōn ginesthai anakypsate kai eparate tas kephalas hymōn, dioti engizei hē apolytrōsis hymōn.

i18n.en: Now when these things begin to take place, straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen parabolēn autois· Idete tēn sykēn kai panta ta dendra·

i18n.en: And he told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree, and all the trees;

paragraphs.text: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: hotan probalōsin ēdē, blepontes aph’ heautōn ginōskete hoti ēdē engys to theros estin·

i18n.en: as soon as they put forth leaves, you see for yourselves and know that the summer is already near.

paragraphs.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, hotan idēte tauta ginomena, ginōskete hoti engys estin hē basileia tou theou.

i18n.en: So also you, when you see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.

paragraphs.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē parelthē hē genea hautē heōs an panta genētai.

i18n.en: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all has taken place.

notes.official: **MAJOR THEOLOGICAL-INTERPRETIVE CRUX — *hē genea hautē* ('this generation').** The eschatological-imminence saying. Five reading-strata preserved: (i) the literal-imminent reading (this 30-40-year generation, fully-fulfilled by 70 CE temple-destruction); (ii) the generation-of-the-end reading (whichever generation sees the signs); (iii) the Jewish-people reading (the Jewish nation as a race / lineage); (iv) the human-race-broadly reading; (v) the type-of-people reading (this kind of unbelieving generation). Marcus AB 2009; Nolland WBC 1993; Fitzmyer AB 1985; Bovon Hermeneia 2012; France NIGTC 2002 all document the contested-interpretive history. The saying is one of the most-discussed NT-eschatology cruxes and central to the historical-Jesus eschatological-imminence question. Documented at the overlay-glossary entry `luke-21-32-genea-haute-this-generation-multi-reading-strata-convention`.

paragraphs.text: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
paragraphs.translit: ho ouranos kai hē gē pareleusontai, hoi de logoi mou ou mē pareleusontai.

i18n.en: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

paragraphs.text: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete de heautois mēpote barēthōsin hymōn hai kardiai en kraipalē kai methē kai merimnais biōtikais, kai epistē eph’ hymas aiphnidios hē hēmera ekeinē

i18n.en: But take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the cares of life, and that day come upon you suddenly,

paragraphs.text: ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hōs pagis· epeiseleusetai gar epi pantas tous kathēmenous epi prosōpon pasēs tēs gēs.

i18n.en: like a snare; for it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.

paragraphs.text: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: agrypneite de en panti kairō deomenoi hina katischysēte ekphygein tauta panta ta mellonta ginesthai, kai stathēnai emprosthen tou huiou tou anthrōpou.

i18n.en: But watch at every time, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man."

paragraphs.text: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de tas hēmeras en tō hierō didaskōn, tas de nyktas exerchomenos ēulizeto eis to oros to kaloumenon Elaiōn·

i18n.en: And during the day he was teaching in the temple, but at night he would go out and lodge on the mount called Olivet.

paragraphs.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas ho laos ōrthrizen pros auton en tō hierō akouein autou.

i18n.en: And all the people came to him early in the morning in the temple to hear him.
